pr_title: [wasi] Bundle `runtimeconfig` in the single file bundle
pr_body:
This removes the need for having access to a local filesystem for reading the runtimeconfig . Thus the app can be run with `wasmtime run foo.wasm`.

- [wasi] WasiAppBuilder: error out for single file bundles, if there ..
- [wasi] driver.c: bundle runtimeconfig.bin, and use that for the single file bundle case
- [wasi] Don't add '--dir' for single file bundles

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/94407 .

issue_context.title: Enabling InvariantGlobalization breaks int.Parse in WASI apps
issue_context.body:
### Description

While enabling InvariantGlobalization makes the size of the binary much smaller, int.Parse (and its friends) throw when used in that mode. This shouldn't be the case according to the offical docs: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/design/features/globalization-invariant-mode.md

It seems like mono is not aware of the `InvariantGlobalization` being enabled when compiling to a single binary. Please note that `runtimeconfig.json` is not a suitable solution because WASI apps don't necessarily have access to the file system

### Reproduction Steps

csproj:

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <RuntimeIdentifier>wasi-wasm</RuntimeIdentifier>
    <OutputType>Exe</OutputType>
    <PublishTrimmed>true</PublishTrimmed>

    <WasmSingleFileBundle>true</WasmSingleFileBundle>
    <InvariantGlobalization>true</InvariantGlobalization>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

Program.cs:
```csharp
using System;
using System.Globalization;

var n = int.Parse("1", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
Console.WriteLine($"Number: {n}");
```

### Expected behavior

It should print out "Number: 1"

### Actual behavior

```
wasmtime run .\bin\Debug\net8.0\wasi-wasm\AppBundle\SizeApp.wasm
[MONO] warning: Process terminated.
[MONO] warning: Couldn't find a valid ICU package installed on the system. Please install libicu (or icu-libs) using your package manager and try again. Alternatively you can set the configuration flag System.Globalization.Invariant to true if you want to run with no globalization support. Please see https://aka.ms/dotnet-missing-libicu for more information.
```
